decisions.reason: The enclosure must retain the power board during a drop, but the source does not change the board's dimensions, orientation, mounting holes, connector clearance, or other mechanical attributes.
Simple enclosure assembly and component retention do not entail any change to connector placement, orientation, alignment, or cable routing.
The enclosure assembly and drop-retention constraints do not alter ESP32 pin coverage, breakout placement, breakout format, or platform purpose.
Requiring the enclosure to secure the sensor board does not change the existing requirement that all sensor-board components and connectors fit on the board.
The source does not change the ESP32 antenna's required placement at the PCB edge or specify a new RF-clearance constraint.
The enclosure must accommodate and secure the existing components, but the source does not change the three-board architecture or any board role.
The enclosure requirements do not modify the main board's adjustable prototype dimensions or its specified 70 by 50 mm size.
Enclosure assembly and component retention do not affect the power board's layer count or grounding strategy.
The mechanical enclosure decision does not change the JLCPCB order setup, actors, missing-part handling, or order grouping.
Although the button is panel-mounted, the source does not change its connector, board location, electrical connection, mounting type, or switch behavior.
The enclosure's physical assembly and retention requirements do not change BOM part-number or board-specific BOM requirements.
The enclosure assembly and drop-retention constraints do not alter the requirement for lead-free PCB manufacturing.
